visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: A buyer on 20x earnings buys a target at 15x (at the offer price), all in shares, with no synergies. Accretive or dilutive?

options.text: Dilutive, since the buyer pays a premium
Neutral, since no synergies are assumed

questions.explain: The target's earnings yield at the offer price is 1 ÷ 15 ≈ 6.7%; the buyer's shares cost 1 ÷ 20 = 5%. It earns more than the money costs, so EPS rises.
questions.explain_at: Then the target's earnings yield at the offer price

questions.q: Atlas borrows €150m at 6% with a 25% tax rate. What does the interest cost after tax?
questions.explain: €150m × 6% = €9m of interest, but interest is tax-deductible, so it costs €9m × 75% = €6.75m. Using the full €9m was Sofia's slip.
questions.explain_at: Interest is paid before tax, so the taxman pays part of it

questions.q: What does an accretive deal tell you about value?

options.text: Little on its own: EPS ignores price and risk
That the buyer paid less than fair value
That the synergies cover the premium paid
That it's a good deal for shareholders

questions.explain: Cheap debt makes almost any purchase accretive: Atlas could pay about 22x with debt and still raise EPS. EPS ignores the price relative to value, risk and growth.
questions.explain_at: Earnings per share ignores the price relative to value

questions.q: What did Microsoft say LinkedIn would do to its adjusted EPS at first?
questions.explain: About 1% dilution for the rest of financial year 2017 and for 2018, turning accretive in financial year 2019. Microsoft was paying for growth.
questions.explain_at: Microsoft expected the deal to dilute its adjusted earnings per share by about one percent

questions.q: ZO Skin Health has an enterprise value of $1.5bn and net sales of about $330m. Roughly what multiple is that?
questions.explain: $1.5bn ÷ $330m ≈ 4.5x. It's a revenue multiple; the release gives no profit figure, so calling it an earnings multiple is wrong.
questions.explain_at: That's right, and it's a revenue multiple
